City Council

Title: Electric Generation Vapor Compressor – Sole Source Purchase Order
Contact: Nathan Ribordy, Steve Hancock 916-746-1673, 916-774-5631 nribordy@roseville.ca.us,
sjhancock@roseville.ca.us
SUMMARY
Staff recommends approval of a Sole Source Purchase Order with American Compressor Company in the
amount of $341,314.92 to provide two (2) Howden Roots manufactured rotary lobe vapor compressors for
onsite backup inventory replacing the prior backup inventory which are now in service. Funding is included
in the Electric Department’s Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget in the Electric Fund.
RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council approve a sole source purchase order with American Compressor
Company for two Howden Roots manufactured rotary lobe vapor compressors.
BACKGROUND
The Roseville Energy Park (REP) uses a Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) system to process waste streams
and reduce liquid waste. Rotary lobe vapor compressors are used in the ZLD to increase the efficiency of
the process. The ZLD vapor compressors are exposed to high chlorides content water, high temperatures
and continuous service. These operating conditions cause erosion and other maintenance issues which
staff contends with regularly. The current vapor compressors have been replaced with the backup stock of
compressors. The requested vapor compressors will replace the backup stock which are now in use. This
backup stock of compressors will be ready to install as needed without any extended wait times.
The rotary lobe vapor compressors that are installed are Howden Roots Model 1216 RGS. American
Compressor Company is the sole factory authorized distributor of the vapor compressor model used in the
REP Zero Liquid Discharge process. Because of this, staff recommends the approval of Sole Source
purchase of two rotary lobe vapor compressors from American Compressor Company.
FISCAL IMPACT
The total cost of services will not exceed $341,314.92. Funding is included in the Electric Department's
Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget in the Electric Fund.
ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW
The California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) only applies to projects which have the potential to
cause a significant effect on the environment. Where it can be seen with certainty that there is no
possibility that the activity in question may have a significant effect on the environment, the activity is not
subject to CEQA. (CEQA Guidelines §15061(b)(3)). The approval of this sole source purchase order with
American Compressor Company meets this requirement and is not subject to CEQA. No additional CEQA
review is necessary.

Staff recommends approval of a sole source purchase order with Motorola Solutions, Inc. in the amount of
$501,037.50 to provide All Band Portable Radios. Motorola Solutions, Inc. is the manufacturer of the APX
8000 All Band Protable Radio, which contains proprietary hardware and software components that are only
available through Motorola. Funding for this purchase was included in the adopted FY2026-27 budget in
the Police Portable Radio Replacement project in the Equipment Replacement Fund.
RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council approve a sole source purchase order to Motorola Solutions, Inc.
for the purchase of 50 All Band Portable Radios in the amount of $501,037.50.

The Roseville Police Department has relied on Motorola Solutions portable radios for over 20 years to
ensure effective communication for public safety operations. The department currently has (93) APX 7000
portable radios, many of which have been in service since 2010. These units have reached the end of their
operational life, as Motorola Solutions no longer manufactures the APX 7000 model or provides parts and
accessories for its maintenance. The Police Department is currently in the second year of a three-year
plan to replace all APX 7000 portable radios with the Motorola Solutions APX 8000 All Band Portable
Radio. The APX 8000 radio meets the Police Department's need for reliable, secure, and interoperable
communication. The purchase of (50) APX 8000 radios will replace the department's oldest units.
Motorola Solutions, Inc. is the manufacturer of the APX 8000 All Band Portable Radio, which contains
proprietary hardware and software components that are only available through Motorola Solutions, Inc.

The total cost of this Portable Radio purchase is $501,037.50. Funding of $500,000 for this purchase was
included in the adopted FY2026-27 budget in the Police Portable Radio Replacement project in the
Equipment Replacement Fund. The remaining amount of $1,037.50 will come from the Police
Department's FY2026-27 budget in the General Fund.

or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment, or is otherwise not considered a

purchase order for the purchase of radios meets the above criteria and is not subject to CEQA. No
additional environmental review is required.

Title: Ultraviolet Disinfection Equipment – Sole Source Annual Purchase Order
Contact: Katherine Gettings 916-746-1865 kgettings@roseville.ca.us
SUMMARY
Staff recommends approval of a sole source purchase order including four (4) additional one-year
renewals with Trojan Technologies Corp. for supply of repair parts and replacement components for the
ultraviolet disinfection system at the Dry Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant and Pleasant Grove
Wastewater Treatment Plant. Trojan Technologies Corp. is the sole supplier of validated replacement parts
required to maintain system performance and meet regulatory requirements. The total cost of the purchase
order is not to exceed $1,000,000 per year with a total of $5,000,000 over five years. Funding will be
provided from the Environmental Utilities Department’s annual approved budgets for the Wastewater
Operations Fund.
RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council adopt a resolution approving a sole source purchase order with
Trojan Technologies Corp. for supply of repair parts and replacement components for the ultraviolet (UV)
disinfection system at the Dry Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant (DCWWTP) and Pleasant Grove
Wastewater Treatment Plant (PGWWTP) and authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute four
(4) additional one (1) year renewals for purchase orders without further City Council approval, provided
that the applicable budget is approved by the City Council each year, or until City staff determines that
continuing with the same vendor is not in the City's best interest.
BACKGROUND
Wastewater at the Dry Creek Watewater Treatment Plant (DCWWTP) and the Pleasant Grove Wastewater
Treatment Plant (PGWWTP) is treated through primary, secondary, and tertiary processes and then
disinfected using ultraviolet (UV) systems manufactured by Trojan Technologies Corp. The disinfected
water is either reused as Title 22 recycled water or discharged to local creeks, making reliable UV system
performance essential for compliance with the City’s National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System
(NPDES) and recycled water permit requirements. Both treatment plants utilize Trojan 3000 systems that
require routine maintenance and periodic replacement of key components such as lamps, sensors,
ballasts, and wiper mechanisms, which have reached the end of their service life and are experiencing
increased failures. The proposed annual purchase order will support ongoing maintenance and
programmatic replacement of these components. Trojan Technologies Corp. is the sole supplier of
validated replacement parts required to maintain system performance and meet regulatory requirements.
FISCAL IMPACT
The estimated cost is $1,000,000 for FY2026-27, $1,000,000 for FY2027-28, $1,000,000 for FY2028-29,
$1,000,000 for FY2029-30, and $1,000,000 for FY2030-31. The total not-to-exceed cost for the purchase
orders, including the four additional one-year renewals, is $5,000,000. Funding will be provided from the
Environmental Utilities Department’s annual budgets in the Wastewater Operations Fund.
ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW
The California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) does not apply to activities that will not result in a direct
or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment, or is otherwise not considered a
project as defined by CEQA Statute §21065 and CEQA State Guidelines §15060(c)(3) and §15378.
A purchase order for Trojan Technologies Corp. equipment does not include the potential for a significant
environmental effect, and therefore is not subject to CEQA.

SUMMARY
Staff recommends approval of a sole source purchase order with Thirkettle Corporation dba Aqua Metric
Sales Company for Sensus water meters and related parts for $950,000 in FY2026-27. In addition, staff
requests this purchase order be renewed annually as follows, subject to budget approval: FY2027-28
estimated at $980,000; FY2028-29 estimated at $1,010,000; and FY2029-30 estimated at $1,045,000, for

Thirkettle Corporation dba Aqua Metric Sales Company for Sensus water meters and related parts for
$950,000 in FY2026-27, and further authorize three (3) additional one (1) year renewals without further

BACKGROUND
There are approximately 56,000 meters in the City's water distribution system. The Environmental Utilities
Department (EU) uses Sensus water meters for all domestic, commercial, and irrigation consumption. This

continuing this product line because Sensus meters have proven reliable over the last 31 years and costs
related to staff training, labor, and materials will be predictable and minimized. EU's water utility regularly
reviews other manufacturers, but trials have resulted in unacceptable failure rates and potential issues
related to unproven technology. The only authorized local representative for Sensus meters is Thirkettle
Corporation dba Aqua-Metric Sales Company, who provides excellent customer service and works closely
with EU's water utility staff on all orders, including delivering critical products on short notice in emergency

Corporation dba Aqua-Metric Sales Company will be from appropriations in the Water Operations Fund

SUMMARY
Staff recommends approval of a change order for import tariffs to the sole source purchase order with
Siebtechnik Tema for centrifuge dewatering equipment at the Roseville Energy Park and to grant Electric
staff the authority to approve unforeseen change orders up to 10% of the equipment cost. The total cost of
the change order is $75,052.84. The new total cost of the purchase order including 10% contingency is
$636,385.82. Funding is included in the Electric Department's FY2025-26 budget in the Electric Fund.
RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council adopt a resolution to approve a change order to the sole source
purchase order to Siebtechnik Tema for centrifuge dewatering equipment import tariffs.
Staff further recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager or his designee is authorized to
approve change orders, consisting with the contract terms, provided that the net cost of all change orders
shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the total contract price.
BACKGROUND
The Roseville Energy Park (REP) utilizes a Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) system to make demineralized
water and treat process waste streams. The final treatment step in the ZLD is dewatering slurry from two
crystallizers to produce dry salt cake that is hauled to the local landfill. The dewatering treatment step is
currently performed by a single belt filter press originally installed during the ZLD construction in 2006.
The existing belt press is a single point of failure and offers no redundancy when failure often occurs, it is
severely undersized restricting ZLD processing capacity, it inefficiently dewaters slurry in batch feeds
rather than a continuous feed, and after many repairs and improvements the belt press is at end of life.
Through the rigorous engineering and operational testing conducted onsite at the REP with multiple
equipment types and vendors, centrifuge technology by Siebtechnik Tema was selected. A sole source
purchase order with Siebtechnik Tema was previously approved by City Council at the December 18,
2024, meeting by Resolution 24-419. The estimated centrifuge fabrication time was approximately 12
months. The centrifuge fabrication is now complete and ready for shipment from Germany to Roseville.
The centrifuge and associated costs were $510,302.71 in December 2024. An additional 10%
contingency was granted for unforeseen change orders of $51,030.27, for a total budget authority of
$561,332.98. Siebtechnik Tema manufactures their centrifuges in Germany. From December 2024 to
today, tariff costs between Germany and the United States have increased significantly. The tariff
surcharge for this equipment is $69,654.60 plus $5,398.24 in taxes, for a total additional cost of
$75,052.84.
As this change order amount exceeds the remaining authorized contingency amount, staff is requesting
approval from City Council to increase the contract authority by the tariff cost, to a new total of
$636,385.82. The remaining contingency funds are intended to remain for unforeseen costs during
installation and commissioning.
FISCAL IMPACT
The total cost of one centrifuge, estimated freight, 10% contingency, and sales tax is now $636,385.82,
including the $75,052.84 import tariff. Funding is included in the Electric Department's FY2025-26 budget
in the Electric Fund.
ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW
The proposed project involves operational minor alterations of an existing facility. This activity is
categorically exempt from CEQA as a Class 1 Exemption (State CEQA Guidelines Section 15301). The
Exemption has been prepared and no further CEQA action is required.

SUMMARY
Staff recommends approval of a sole source open purchase order including four (4) additional one-year
renewals with Placer County Water Agency for water services to Roseville customers in Stoneridge
Specific Plan. Placer County Water Agency is the sole supplier of water services in portions of the
Stoneridge Specific Plan. The total cost of the purchase order is not to exceed $764,000 over five years.
Funding will be provided from the annual budgets of the Parks, Recreation & Libraries Department in the
General Fund and Stoneridge Community Facilities District No. 1 (Services District).
RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council adopt a resolution to approve a sole source open purchase order
with Placer County Water Agency for water services and authorize the City Manager to execute it on
behalf of the City of Roseville. Additionally, staff requests authority for the City Manager or his designee to
execute four (4) additional one (1) year renewals without further City Council approval, provided that the
applicable budget is approved by the City Council each year, or until staff determines that continuing with
the same vendor is not in the City’s best interest.
BACKGROUND
In 1993, the City enlisted the help of SPINK Corporation to develop a water system master plan. This plan
identified four different pressure zones needed to provide adequate service to Roseville customers. The
Stoneridge Specific Plan is situated over two of the higher-pressure zones. Water supply for a good portion
of the specific plan was to be provided by Placer County Water Agency (PCWA).
In reviewing the proposed specific plan infrastructure, staff felt that the most economical way to provide
service to the highest-pressure zone would be to work with PCWA. Using PCWA infrastructure and system
elevation minimizes the amount of pumping required to service high-pressure zones.
To accomplish this, PCWA and the City entered into an agreement in March 1998 (Reso #2067) to
exchange service areas of similar sizes. The City provides service in the lower areas and PCWA provides
service in the higher elevation areas. These service area exchanges are located within the Stoneridge
Specific Plan.
Historically, the City paid PCWA for these services using the payment request form process. Beginning in
FY 2024–25, staff transitioned to using purchase orders to improve cost tracking and financial
transparency. Due to continued increases in water service rates, the total annual expenditures now exceed
the City Council’s spending authorization limit.

source purchase is necessary because the industry has transitioned to trailers, and the Electric department
works in alleys and narrow areas in new construction that limits the size of a trailer. Envoltz is the sole
manufacturer and distributor, and has proprietary designs and subsystems. The vehicle is a business
necessity that provides the specialized equipment required to safely install, replace, and maintain the
City's underground electric distribution system. The Envoltz cable pulling equipment is essential for
installing underground primary and secondary electrical cables on new construction projects, replacing
aging infrastructure, and performing emergency repairs to restore electric service.
During the production of an Envoltz truck, it is common to encounter unanticipated or changed conditions
which necessitate minor additions or other modifications to the project and the contract. Due to the
complexity of the build, the Fleet Manager requests authorization for the City Manager or his designee to
approve change order requests in an amount not to exceed 1% of the contract price, or $3,309.87, or the
remaining portion of the approved budget (if lesser).

Purchase Agreement
Contact: Kate Rebello 916-774-5945 krebello@roseville.ca.us
SUMMARY
Staff recommends approval of a sole-source contract purchase agreement with Gallup, Inc. in the amount
of $100,000 for a 4.5-day, onsite CliftonStrengths and Gallup Global Strengths Coach training course for
thirty employees, to be conducted October 12-16, 2026. Gallup, Inc. is the sole organization authorized to
teach, certify, and license the CliftonStrengths Global Strengths Coach curriculum. Funding for these
services is included in the City Manager's Department budget in the General Fund.
RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council adopt a resolution to approve a contract purchase agreement
(3005533) with Gallup, Inc. for an on-site CliftonStrengths and Gallup Global Strengths Coach training
course.
BACKGROUND
Gallup, Inc. is the sole organization authorized to teach, certify, and license the CliftonStrengths Global
Strengths Coach curriculum. Through this agreement, Gallup will provide instructor-led CliftonStrengths
training, including course materials, to support the City’s leadership and organizational development
initiatives. The 4.5-day, onsite CliftonStrengths and Gallup Global Strengths Coach training course for
thirty employees will be conducted October 12-16, 2026.
Gallup’s CliftonStrengths methodology is grounded in decades of research in positive psychology and is
designed to help individuals, teams, and organizations identify and develop their natural strengths. The
program supports key organizational priorities by fostering employee engagement, improving team
effectiveness, enhancing leadership development, and promoting overall workplace wellbeing.
Organizations that have implemented strengths-based development have reported improvements in
employee engagement, retention, productivity, customer engagement, and overall organizational
performance.
The training also provides leaders, managers, and employees with the tools and coaching needed to
integrate a strengths-based approach into the City’s culture, creating opportunities for ongoing
development, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
FISCAL IMPACT
Funding for these services is included in the City Manager's Department budget in the General Fund for
Fiscal Year 2026-27. The contract amount is not to exceed $100,000.

The California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) does not apply to activities that will not result in a direct
or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment or is otherwise not considered a
project as defined by CEQA Statute §21065 and CEQA State Guidelines §15060(c)(3) and §15378.
Approval of the Grants Advisory Commission funding recommendations meet the above criteria and are
not subject to CEQA. No additional environmental review is required.

Title: Electronic Plan Review - Sole Source Agreement
Contact: Chris Fanucchi 916-746-1353 CFanucchi@roseville.ca.us
SUMMARY
Staff recommends approval of a sole source agreement with Lifecycle Technologies, LLC dba LCT
Software for access to its cloud-based electronic plan review platform, DigEplan, with a not-to-exceed
(NTE) amount of $63,953 for the initial term and a total NTE amount of $210,193 over the full three-year
term, including renewal options. Funding is included in the Development Services Department’s
Technology Replacement Fund, which is funded through permit fees designated for development-driven
technology improvements, and is included in the Department's FY2025–26 budget. Approval of the
agreement will have no net fiscal impact on the General Fund. Staff also recommends authorization for the
City Manager to execute future amendments to extend the agreement for up to two (2) additional one (1)
year renewal terms on behalf of the City.
RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council adopt a resolution to approve a Sole Source Agreement with
Lifecycle Technologies, LLC dba LCT Software for the electronic plan review platform, DigEplan, and
authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement on behalf of the City of Roseville.
Staff additionally requests authority for the City Manager or his designee to execute two (2) additional one
(1) year renewals without further City Council approval, provided that the applicable budget is approved by
the City Council, or until staff determines that continuing with this vendor is not in the best interest of the
City.
BACKGROUND
In March 2020, the City Council approved an agreement with LCT Software (then licensed under TruePoint
Solutions LLC) following a formal Request for Proposal (RFP) process for electronic plan review software.
The software was selected to support the City’s transition from paper-based plan review processes to a
fully electronic plan review environment integrated with the City’s enterprise permitting system, Accela.
Since then, the Development Services Department has utilized DigEplan, a cloud-based electronic plan
review platform, to enable City staff and contracted third-party plan reviewers to electronically review, mark
up, and approve construction plans and supporting documents directly within the City's permitting system.
The integrated platform streamlines the review process while providing applicants with clear, consistent,
and standardized feedback on their plan submissions.
Staff recommends continuing with LCT Software on a sole-source basis because DigEplan is fully
integrated with the City’s Accela permitting system and has become a critical component of the
Department’s electronic plan review workflow. Over the past five years, staff, consultants, and customers
have established business processes and workflows around the platform. Transitioning to an alternative
solution would require significant staff time and resources to evaluate, procure, configure, test, and
implement a replacement platform, as well as retrain staff, consultants, and customers. Staff has
determined that renewing the agreement with LCT Software is the most cost-effective and operationally
efficient option for maintaining continuity of service and minimizing disruption to permit processing
operations.
FISCAL IMPACT
The agreement includes a not-to-exceed (NTE) amount of $63,953 for the initial term, $70,620 for the first
renewal term, and $75,620 for the second renewal term, for a total NTE amount of $210,193 over three (3)
years. Funding is included in the Development Services Department’s Technology Replacement Fund,
which is funded through permit fees designated for development-driven technology improvements. As a
result, approval of the agreement will have no net fiscal impact on the General Fund. Funding for FY2025–
26 is included in the Department’s budget.
ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW
The California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) only applies to projects which have the potential to
cause a significant effect on the environment. Where it can be seen with certainty that there is no
possibility that the activity in question may have a significant effect on the environment, the activity is not
subject to CEQA (CEQA Guidelines §15061(b)(3)). No additional environmental review is required.

Title: Wastewater Climber Screens Parts and Equipment – Sole Source Purchase Order

SUMMARY
Staff recommends approval of a sole source purchase order with Veolia WTS Services USA, Inc. to provide
repair parts and replacement equipment for the Influent Climber Screens at the Dry Creek Wastewater
Treatment Plant and the Pleasant Grove Wastewater Treatment Plant for $300,000, and the option to
execute four additional one-year $300,000 renewals for a total not to exceed $1,500,000. Funding will be
provided from the Environmental Utilities Department’s annual budgets in the Wastewater Operations
Fund.
RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommend that the City Council adopt a resolution to approve a sole source purchase order with
Veolia WTS Services USA, Inc. to provide repair parts and replacement equipment for the Influent Climber
Screens at the Dry Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant (DCWWTP) and the Pleasant Grove Wastewater
Treatment Plant (PGWWTP), and authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute four (4) additional
one (1) year purchase order renewals without further City Council approval, provided that the applicable
budget is approved by the City Council each year, or until City staff determines that continuing with the
same vendor is not in the City's best interest.
BACKGROUND
The Environmental Utilities Department (EUD) has five (5) influent climber screens (mechanical bar
screens) at DCWWTP and PGWWTP. Climber screens are used to remove large debris in the initial step of
the treatment process. Each climber screen is custom designed for the wastewater treatment plants’
influent needs and configuration. Veolia WTS Services USA Inc. is the original equipment manufacturer
and sole provider of repair parts and replacement equipment for the climber units. EUD is recommending a
one-year purchase order with Veolia for both DCWWTP and PGWWTP, with four optional renewal years at
one-year intervals for a total of five (5) years.
FISCAL IMPACT
The estimated cost is $300,000 for year one; $300,000 for year two; $300,000 for year three; $300,000 for
year four; and $300,000 for year five. The total not-to-exceed cost for the purchase orders including the
four additional one (1) year renewals is $1,500,000. Funding will be provided from the Environmental
Utilities Department’s annual budgets in the Wastewater Operations Fund.
ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW
The California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) does not apply to activities that will not result in a direct
or reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment, or is otherwise not considered a
project as defined by CEQA Statute §21065 and CEQA State Guidelines §15060(c)(3) and §15378.
The purchase of wastewater influent climber screens parts and equipment meets the above criteria and is
not subject to CEQA. No additional environmental review is required.
